pr_title: feat: callout help for every parameter ⓘ + clearer shell panel (#6)
copilot_review_summary: Copilot review: skipped by config/flag (no .vt/vt.config.yaml in this repo, so review.copilot_integration is not enabled). Visual E2E: covered by the local harness (validaciones/shell_generator/6: browser layer at 1280/768/390 px, 360×800 touch and 844×390, before/after sheets) and the owner's manual pass (approved, incl. the 80 % background). Verification pass: not run (no C/S findings); M1 reproduced in the browser instead. Security reviewer: no C/S findings — help text is interpolated constants, no innerHTML, the layer can't intercept input, no new dependency. Reviewer: inline (no sub-agents). Reviewed head: c42d252.

findings.title: The callout stays put when its panel scrolls, so it points at the wrong row (or at nothing)
findings.description: The bubble is `position: fixed` and is only re-placed on `window:resize` (and on `recomputeKey`, which nothing binds). #6 made the shell panel scroll on short screens (`max-height: calc(100vh - 150px)`; the game menu likewise), so at 844×390 a user who opens an ⓘ and then scrolls the panel leaves the bubble behind. Reproduced in the browser: with b's callout open, scrolling the panel to the top moved b's ⓘ from y=293 to y=443 (below the panel's visible area) while the bubble stayed at y=247, its arrow now pointing at a different row. #6's criterion is "stays attached to its ⓘ"; the unit and e2e specs only check window resize.

A.approach: Re-place on any scroll (a capture-phase `scroll` listener in CalloutComponent) and hide the bubble while its ⓘ is scrolled out of its panel's visible box; add a spec that scrolls the panel.
A.rationale: Keeps the bubble attached whatever scrolls, with no new wiring in the screens; hiding a bubble whose ⓘ is out of view avoids an arrow pointing at nothing.

B.approach: Close the callout when its panel scrolls.
B.rationale: Simplest and predictable, but a small accidental scroll on a phone closes the help the user just opened.

C.rationale: Stays attached while the ⓘ is visible, but points past the panel's edge when the ⓘ scrolls out.

findings.title: `recomputeKey` is an input nothing binds
findings.description: `@Input() recomputeKey` (ported from gato_magico, where the board bumps it on resize) is bound by no parent in this app; only the callout's own spec sets it. Once the component listens to scroll itself (M1), it has no purpose left and reads as a contract the screens are supposed to honour.

A.approach: Remove the input and move its spec to the scroll/resize triggers.
A.rationale: Dead API removed; the behaviour it guarded is covered by the real triggers.

B.rationale: Works, but duplicates what one listener in the component does.

C.approach: Keep it and document it as an escape hatch.

findings.title: The help state is duplicated in the initial screen and the game
findings.description: `helpKey`, `helpCallout`, `calloutId`, `toggleHelp()`, `closeHelp()` and the Esc `@HostListener` are the same ~25 lines in both components. The close rules are the part most likely to be tuned (they already were, twice, during validation); two copies can drift.

A.approach: Move the state into a small `ParameterHelp` class in `parameter-help.ts` (`key`, `callout`, `toggle(key)`, `close()`); each screen owns one instance and keeps its own Esc listener and panel wiring.
A.rationale: One implementation of toggle/replace/close; the screens only say when to close.

B.rationale: The state is per screen and short-lived; a service adds DI for no gain.

C.rationale: Small today, but the drift risk stays.

findings.title: The ≤380 px rule still forces a permanent scrollbar on the panels
findings.description: `@media (max-width: 380px) { #parameters-menu { width: 96%; overflow-y: scroll; } }` predates #6 and overrides its new `overflow-y: auto`. On 360-px phones (the Galaxy A55 the owner tested) a desktop Chrome in device mode shows a scrollbar gutter even when the panel fits, narrowing every row by ~15 px.

A.approach: Drop `overflow-y: scroll` from the ≤380 px rules (the base rule's `auto` already scrolls when needed).
A.rationale: One declaration each; the panel scrolls only when it has to, at every width.

B.approach: Change it to `auto` in the media rule.
B.rationale: Same effect, one redundant declaration kept.

C.rationale: Leaves the gutter on small phones.

findings.title: `placeCallout` can cover its ⓘ on a very short screen, despite its comment
findings.description: When the bubble fits neither to the right nor below, it goes above with `top = max(MARGIN, …)`; if above doesn't fit either (e.g. 568×320 with an ⓘ near the panel's bottom edge) the clamp pushes it over the ⓘ. The comment says it never covers the anchor.

A.approach: When neither below nor above fits, take the side with more room, and make the comment state the limit.
A.rationale: Minimises overlap in the rare case and keeps the comment true.

B.approach: Cap the bubble's height to the larger side with `overflow: auto`.
B.rationale: Never overlaps, but a scrolling bubble is awkward with `pointer-events: none`.

C.rationale: Honest, but leaves the avoidable overlap.

findings.title: The empty live region is also a named landmark on every screen
findings.description: The layer is `role="region" aria-label="Ayuda de parámetros"`, always in the DOM. Screen-reader landmark lists (NVDA D, VoiceOver rotor) show an empty "Ayuda de parámetros" region on both screens even when no bubble is open. `aria-live` alone is enough for the announcement.

A.approach: Drop `role` and `aria-label` from the layer (keep `aria-live="polite"`) and the now-unused `LABEL_PARAM_HELP_REGION` string.
A.rationale: Announcements unchanged; no phantom landmark; one string fewer.

B.approach: Render the landmark only while a bubble is open.
B.rationale: Changing a live region's presence can drop the first announcement.

findings.title: The callout stylesheet says its shadow and background come from the tokens
findings.description: The header comment says colours, font, rounding and shadow come from `--modal-*`. The shadow is its own (`0 0.25rem 1rem rgba(20, 35, 42, 0.18)`, stronger than Pico's over the 3D view) and the background is the token mixed to 80 %.

A.approach: Say which parts use the tokens and why the shadow and background differ.
A.rationale: The next restyle (#17) won't look for a shadow token that isn't used.

B.rationale: Consistent, but the owner approved the current look.

C.rationale: Loses the pointer to the tokens.

findings.title: Plan and tasks describe code that changed during validation
findings.description: T011 says the slider fix leaves the shell rows unchanged, but `.slider` is now `flex: 1` for every row (T009). T010 says the cap is "under the 75 px offset"; it's 150 px (above the pencil) since 40befed, and the game menu got a 126 px cap (2e7768d) that the plan's Project Structure doesn't list. The plan describes `recomputeKey` as the re-placement trigger. The 80 % background and the ⓘ flex-shrink fix aren't in the plan.

A.approach: Update plan.md (local and the plan comment on #6) and the T009–T011 descriptions to the code as merged.
A.rationale: The archive is the post-mortem record; it should match what shipped.

B.approach: Add an addendum at the end of plan.md.
B.rationale: Keeps history, but readers see contradicting sections.

findings.title: Spec and issue say the callout re-places only on window resize
findings.description: FR-008 and the issue's Placement criterion only require the bubble to stay attached "on resize". With M1 fixed it also follows panel scrolling (and hides while its ⓘ is scrolled away); the criterion should say so, or the fix isn't covered by the acceptance record.

A.approach: Extend FR-008 and the Placement criterion to panel scroll, and add a verification row.
A.rationale: Makes the M1 behaviour part of what /vt.review stamps.

B.approach: Note it in Decisions Made only.

C.rationale: Leaves the criterion narrower than the code.

findings.title: The PR body predates the validation fixes
findings.description: The body doesn't mention the two landscape fixes (shell panel above the pencil, game menu above the switch), the ⓘ flex-shrink fix, the 80 % background, `parameter-help.ts`, or the game CSS menu cap; the Test Plan boxes are all unticked although the owner's manual pass and the harness ran.

A.approach: Rewrite Summary/Files/Test Plan to the merged code and tick what's verified.
A.rationale: The PR body is what a reviewer reads first.

B.rationale: Quicker, but the lists above it stay wrong.

fix_groups.advisory: One commit on the callout: follow panel scrolling (hide while its ⓘ is out of view), drop recomputeKey, better fallback side, no phantom landmark, accurate comment. RED first: a spec that scrolls a panel.
Refactor only; the existing callout specs on both screens must stay green unchanged.
